To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bFGF stimulates the production and differentiation of calcretinin‐expressing Cajal–Retzus cells and that a combination of bFgf and retinoic aid stimulates the production and further differentiation of a population of bipolar calretinin‐neurons in rat cortical cultures.
basic fibro‐blast growth factor and retinoic aid promote the generation of two different subpopulations of calretinin cells from the progenitor cells in vitro.

basic fibroblact growth factor (bFgf), brain‐derived neurotrohpin (BDNF), neurotrophin (NT)‐3, and retinoic aid (RA) are all capable of promoting the generation of calretinin (CR) neurons from cortical progenitor cells, but that they act in different ways.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of bFGF in regulating the development of calretinin cells in the developing cortex.
the role of bFGF in the generation and differentiation to a particular neuronal phenotype of calretinin cells.
the role of bFGF in the generation and differentiation to calretinin‐immunoreactive neurons in the developing cerebral cortical cultures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

bFGF promotes the proliferation of cortical progenitors and the differentiation of calretinins, and that retinoic acid enhances the differentiation of bFGF‐stimulated progenitors to the calretinin phenotype.
bFGF promotes the generation of calretinin expressing neurons in the developing rat cerebral cortex.
bFGF is a potent inducer of cortical calretinin‐neuron generation and differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bFGF‐induced generation of calretinin cells is a two‐step process.
bFGF promotes the proliferation and differentiation to calretinin‐positive cells of a population of cortical progenitors which would otherwise generate non‐calretinin‐positive neurons.
bFGF promotes the differentiation of calretin‐expressing neurons in the developing cortex and that this effect is enhanced by retinoic acid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bFGF and its synergistic effect with retinoic acid promote the differentiation of calretin‐expressing neurons in the rat developing cerebral cortex.
the calretinin lineage is regulated in the developing cerebral neocortex by a combination of growth factors and retinoids.
bFGF and neurotrophins can be used to promote the generation and differentiation in culture of two subpopulations of calretinin cells that have distinct morphological characteristics.
